'''Robert D. Hough''' is an American born mathematician specializing in [[number theory]], [[probability]], and [[discrete mathematics]].  He is currently an associate professor of mathematics at [[Stony Brook University]].

== Early life and education ==
Hough holds BS in Math, MS in CS, and PhD in Math degrees from [[Stanford University]]. He completed his PhD under [[Kannan Soundararajan]] in 2012. Hough was a post-doctoral researcher at [[Cambridge University]] and [[Oxford University]] in the United Kingdom working with [[Ben Green (mathematician)|Ben Green]] from 2013 to 2015, and was a post-doctoral member of the [[Institute for Advanced Study]], [[Princeton, New Jersey]] from 2015 to 2016.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Robert Hough's home page |url=https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~rdhough/ |access-date=2024-01-24 |website=www.math.stonybrook.edu}}</ref>

== Career ==
Hough joined [[Stony Brook University]] as an assistant professor in 2016 and has been an associate professor of mathematics since 2022.<ref name=":0" />

==Achievements==

Hough won the [[Mathematical Association of America]]'s [[David P. Robbins Prize]] at the [[Joint Math Meetings]] in 2017.<ref>{{cite web |title=David P. Robbins Prize |url=https://www.maa.org/programs-and-communities/member-communities/maa-awards/writing-awards/robbins-prizes-0#:~:text=Robbins%20Prize%20of%20%245000%20is,must%20be%20written%20in%20English. |website=[[Mathematical Association of America]] |access-date=October 7, 2022 |archive-date=December 1, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201201153703/https://www.maa.org/programs-and-communities/member-communities/maa-awards/writing-awards/robbins-prizes-0#:~:text=Robbins%20Prize%20of%20%245000%20is,must%20be%20written%20in%20English. |url-status=dead }}</ref> The prize was given for finding the solution of a problem imposed by [[Paul Erdős]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Montgomery |first1=Hugh |title=Ten lectures on the interface of analytic number theory and harmonic analysis |date=1994 |publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]] |isbn=978-0821807378}}</ref>

In February 2020, Hough won the [[Sloan Research Fellowship]].<ref>{{cite web |date=February 24, 2020 |title=Mathematics Professor Robert Hough Awarded Sloan Research Fellowship |url=https://news.stonybrook.edu/featuredpost/mathematics-professor-robert-hough-awarded-sloan-research-fellowship/ |access-date=February 24, 2020 |website=Stony Brook News}}</ref> He also won a Trustees Faculty Award from Stony Brook University.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Ritter |first1=Victoria |date=August 8, 2020 |title=Dow alum Hough receives fellowship |url=https://www.ourmidland.com/news/article/Dow-alum-Hough-receives-fellowship-15466440.php |access-date=August 8, 2020 |website=[[Midland Daily News]]}}</ref>
